isa_gate.detail: 1 code object hipv4-amdgcn-amd-amdhsa--gfx906, v_dot8_i32_i4 x480, v_dot8_u32_u4 x0

isa_facts.v_dot8_i32_i4: 8-lane SIGNED 4-bit x SIGNED 4-bit dot (NOT int8 x int4); pinned by tools/dcu/dot8_numeric_probe.cpp
isa_facts.consequence: int8 activations decompose as a = 16*(a>>4) + ((a&15)-8) + 8; needs 2 dot8 per W word (H/L) + 1 sum-w dot8 per W word; per W byte ~4.25 dot8 instructions at M=8

measurement.l2_flush: 64 MB memset between iterations, per-iter event timing
measurement.note: probe ran concurrently with the live vLLM service (4 GPUs at 0.85 util); the in-run fp16 lds_m8 reference measured 388-418 GB/s vs 451 in the original dedicated run -> ~10% environment penalty, does not affect the verdict

numeric_check.note: integer-exact at scale=1; expected ~1e-2 rel error appears only vs real W4-quantized weights (step 2, not run)

reasoning: measured 54 GB/s fp8-equiv is 8x below the go gate and below the fp8 production stream (163 GB/s)

structural bound: v_dot8 is nibble x nibble, so int8 A needs the H/L split -> >=2 dot8 per W byte at M=8 (+1 sum-w per word); even a zero-overhead 2-dot8/B version extrapolates to ~100-115 GB/s fp8-equiv at the measured per-instruction rate
the 600-700 GB/s model in W4-RESEARCH section 0.3 assumed dot8 consumes int8 activations directly; that ISA assumption is false on gfx906
verdict.next: W4 project stops at probe step; no quantization investment; W8A8 sdot4 route (v_dot4_i32_i8, int8 A) remains the only dot-based alternative and was already measured at 300 GB/s class in the model
